newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Challenger sets A$160 mln of warrants.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Challenger sets A$160 mln of warrants.

text.p: Investment bank Challenger International said on Wednesday it would launch A$160 million worth of five-year warrants linked to 10 Australian-listed companies that would be known as Capital Plus Warrants.
The warrants quarantee investors repayment of their initial capital plus any returns from a rise in the portfolio's value.

"The Capital Plus Warrants enable investors to get exposure to shares while having their capital guaranteed, and as there is no brokerage the warrants provide a very cost-efficint entry to the stock market," Challenger Managing Director Bill Ireland said.
Ireland told Reuters Challenger aimed to offer eight separate issues of the warrants, with each series worth about A$20 million.
The first series would open on January 18 and close on February 24. The subsequent series would follow at four to five week intervals.
Each Capital Plus Warrant would be issued at a price of A$1,000, with Challenger aiming to sell 20,000 warrants per issue.

The 10 shares covered by the warrants are Amcor Ltd, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Boral Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, CSR Ltd, GIO Australia Holdings Ltd, Lend Lease Corp Ltd, National Australia Bank Ltd, Southcorp Holdings Ltd and Woolworths Ltd.
Macquarie Bank Ltd is the issuer of the warrants.
Challenger said the return on the first series of five year Capital Plus Warrants would be 140 percent unless the issuer announced a different rate for a particular series prior to its opening.

"At the end of the five-year investment term, the investor has the choice of receiving the portfolio of shares or the cash proceeds by instructing Macquarie Bank to arrange or sell the portfolio on their behalf," Challenger said.
"Should the portfolio of shares be worth less than the original issue price of A$1,000, Macquarie Bank will buy back the shares for A$1,000," it said.
Ireland said the product was aimed mostly at those people wanting the capital-stable nature of a fixed interest investment with the exposure to growth of an equity investment.
